**Findings**

**Blocking — “Generated by default” has no owner, trigger, or failing observation.**  
Failure scenario: an agent follows Phase 5, opens a code PR, notifies the human, and never runs the explainer. Nothing in v3 fails, no hook blocks, no checklist item is currently present, and the kill condition cannot distinguish “0 valuable explainers” from “0 explainers produced.” The spec says “Nothing blocks if it is absent” while still relying on default generation to make the cheap half exist. Anchor: `docs/explainer-spec.md:131-137`, `docs/explainer-spec.md:347-353`, `docs/dev-process.md:92-105`.

**High — Decisions surfaced by the explainer live where ADR reconciliation does not look.**  
Failure scenario: an explainer identifies a hard-to-reverse, surprising trade-off, flags it as an ADR candidate, then remains only in `.explainers/`, which v3 makes gitignored. Phase 6 reads `CONTEXT.md` and `docs/adr/`, not gitignored local HTML; `scripts/check-docs.py`’s advisory decision-marker report scans `docs/superpowers/specs` and `docs/superpowers/plans`, not `.explainers/`. A future architecture review still relitigates the decision. Anchor: `docs/explainer-spec.md:47-48`, `docs/explainer-spec.md:158-161`, `docs/explainer-spec.md:189-191`, `docs/dev-process.md:116-120`, `scripts/check-docs.py:162-174`.

**High — The kill condition is decorative: nobody counts the five, and no observation makes it fail loudly.**  
Failure scenario: by 2026-09-30, three explainers were produced, or six were produced, or none were produced. There is no durable ledger, task, script, roadmap entry, or required review step that knows which world happened; the skill quietly remains installed. This repeats the “rule depends on remembering” shape v3 claims to avoid. Anchor: `docs/explainer-spec.md:307-319`, `docs/dev-process.md:66-73`, `docs/portable-practices.md:84-89`.

**Medium — The Seams table is a heading plus one example, not a reproducible selection rule.**  
Failure scenario: one explainer records only `BlobStore → serve path`; another records every function boundary; another records only nullable unions. All satisfy “one row per module boundary the change crosses” because “module boundary” and “what crosses” are undefined beyond the single example. The existing mandatory category is narrower: nullable/union values crossing module boundaries. Anchor: `docs/explainer-spec.md:146-157`, `docs/process-checklists.md:64-68`.

**Medium — The deferred quiz section records an unbuilt future design inside the live spec.**  
Failure scenario: a later implementer reads v3, sees first-click lock plus blind baseline as “the two defects round 1 found,” and rebuilds a quiz while missing the other quiz/enforcement findings: PR-body assertions, independence attestation, override escape, SHA binding, CI wiring. v3 says the quiz is not built, but stores partial design advice at the same authority as settled decisions. Anchor: `docs/explainer-spec.md:85-97`, `docs/explainer-spec.md:342-343`.

**Low — The title still implies a pre-merge process property the design cannot observe.**  
Failure scenario: the file is called “The Pre-Merge Explainer,” but absence is explicitly non-blocking and unobservable. “Pre-merge” is only a timing instruction, not a property the process can distinguish from “not run.” Anchor: `docs/explainer-spec.md:1`, `docs/explainer-spec.md:8-9`, `docs/explainer-spec.md:136-137`.
